title: Tenant-level SLA-aware slot-binning and usage heuristics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Large tenants on Dedicated pools have heterogeneous request patterns (steady background traffic, periodic spikes, and unpredictable bursts). Current allocation is coarse-grained (slots sized per-GPU bucket) which either wastes capacity or breaches tenant throughput objectives. Goal: create a tenant-focused binning strategy that maps tenant load profiles into discrete slot classes with SLA-aware headroom and per-tenant autoscale heuristics so we can provide explicit throughput guarantees while minimizing committed cost. Key ideas: 1) compute compact per-tenant micro-profiles (p50/p95 latency tokens-per-second, burst-index, tail risk) from 30d traces; 2) classify tenants into slot-bins (steady, bursty, latency-sensitive, throughput-first) and recommend a slot mix; 3) simulate mixing these bins on a pool-level simulator to estimate P95 latency and committed-GPU utilization under target headroom; 4) expose recommendations in Console with expected cost delta and confidence bands; 5) add lightweight runtime enforcement: slot reservation + tenant routing policy + eviction order for soft headroom breaches.
acceptance_criteria: Offline simulator produces stable estimates for expected P95 and utilization for synthetic mixes within ±5% on repeat runs
Per-tenant recommendation API returns slot_bin, recommended_slot_count, expected_monthly_cost_delta, and confidence_score
Console has a new Slot Binning panel showing top 50 tenants with recommended changes and simulated impact
A canary rollout (single dedicated pool) applies recommendations and we measure SLA adherence and realized utilization vs simulation for 7 days
Design doc and data extract queries reviewed and approved by infra/data team
notes: 2025-11-03 - Kickoff: aligned with PM and product on target metrics (P95 latency SLO, cost reduction target 8-15%). Action: data infra to provide 30d request traces aggregated by tenant and model version.
2025-11-06 - Data team (K. Nguyen) delivered sample traces (1M requests/day per pool subset). Observed median burst-index variation is higher than expected for top-10 tenants.
2025-11-08 - Prototype classifier implemented (k-means on normalized p50/p95/burst) in rust-based pipeline. Early clusters: steady (40%), bursty (30%), latency-sensitive (20%), microspikes (10%).

2025-11-10 - Design review notes: PM asks for explicit confidence bands and a 'safety multiplier' to avoid under-provisioning; Security raised low risk but asked to confirm no tenant PII in traces (data pipeline filtered).

2025-11-12 - Trade-off discussion: tighter headroom reduces SLA violations but increases monthly committed GPU cost. Added 'confidence_score' computed by bootstrapping historical traces and a recommended safety multiplier (default 1.25) configurable per-customer.

2025-11-14 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3214 (simulator harness + binning service). Tests included: synthetic mixes and regression check against previous capacity advisor.
2025-11-15 - Blocker: autoscale hook requires tenant routing metadata from infra svc-tenant-map (ENG-217304). Pausing runtime enforcement until dependency resolved.
2025-11-17 - UX mockups landed in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Slot-Binning-Panel (shared with design).
2025-11-18 - Next: schedule canary for pool 'dedicated-eu-1a' and prepare observability dashboards (per-tenant latency, slot occupancy, eviction events).
